_comment: Rail grinding (T-541, a prototype; Drifting, Content, "Rail grinding (task T-541)"). The grind's numbers, read by scripts/driving/rail_grind.gd when a car is made. All proposals for the board's playtest; the GRIND! trick's pay is in combo.json, rail_grind. Units are map units and seconds.
_catch_comment: Locking on, loosened after the board's playtest of 2026-11-06 ("make it easier to snap on the rail"): the car's centre within reach units of the rail's line (was 1.0), up to end_margin past an end (was 0.5), its height from catch_below under to catch_above over the bar (was 0.5 and 0.25; catch_above went to 1.0 in T-542 round 2, see _platform_comment), falling or level, moving along the rail at min_start_speed or more and within max_angle_deg of it (was 45: 60 still keeps a landing straight across from catching).
_reach_comment: T-551 (the grind overhaul): reach widened from 2.0 to 2.5. A grind now starts only while the player holds Space in the air, so a catch is always wanted: a wider reach can't snatch a car that didn't ask for it, and it makes the deliberate catch easier (the board: easier to start). 2.5 is a car length and a half (the drawing is 3 long, 1 wide) on either side of the bar; the 60-degree angle still keeps a crossing landing from catching.
_platform_comment: T-542 round 2 (the board: snapping from a platform was very hard): the window is measured from the bar, so it must reach the whole arc of a first-tier Jump (about 1.03 units over the ground it left): a bar only 0.1 over a rooftop (the 3.1 pick on a 3 platform) was out of reach for most of the arc with catch_above 0.5. 1.0 catches it all along the arc at any height; the creator also lays auto rails 1.0 over the ground under each end, as over the street. The car and the bar are compared at their real heights.
_slide_comment: Sliding: the speed along the rail drops by decel units/s every second; below end_speed the car drops off beside the rail at drop_side_speed. While grinding, A and D spin the car's body at the air turn rate (as in the air); it keeps sliding along the rail whichever way it faces.
_boost_comment: Landing boost (T-548; the board, 2026-11-06: "a set speed boost along the rail" on every landing, then declining). An amount added, not a speed raised to: land_boost units/s on top of the speed along the rail the car lands with, so a fast landing stays faster than a slow one and every landing feels the same push. 4 is about a third of cruise speed (11 units/s, so 15 after a cruise landing): clearly felt, still under the car's top speed of 33. The boost's part then fades at boost_decline units/s every second on top of decel (3 units/s a second in all for its first 2 s), so it is gone after land_boost / boost_decline = 2 s, about the length of a short rail at that speed; after that only decel. A joint between connected pieces is not a landing: no new boost. Proposals for the board's playtest.
_jump_comment: Jump off a rail (T-548; the board, 2026-11-06, replacing the 15-degree diagonal hop): the car leaves where it faces, whatever its travel along the rail (backwards too), at jump_speed units/s flat; the speed along the rail is not kept. 6 is "a bit": about half of cruise speed, so a first-tier Jump (about 0.83 s in the air) carries the car about 5 units. To catch a parallel rail the car must land moving within max_angle_deg (60) of it: facing 45 degrees toward the jump pair's second rail (3.5 units away, reach 2) it goes about 3.5 units sideways and 3.5 along (4.2 units/s along, over min_start_speed), and lands on it. Proposal for the board's playtest.
_overhaul_comment: The grind overhaul (T-551; the board, 2026-11-07, Drifting, Decisions, "The grind overhaul"). Hold Space in the air to tilt; touch a rail while holding it to grind; the grind lasts while Space stays held; letting go launches the car where it faces at jump_speed flat (above, T-548's 6, its momentum gone) and launch_takeoff_speed up. Any car can do it, no power-up. launch_takeoff_speed 5 is the Jump power-up's tier-1 takeoff, the hop T-548's numbers were measured with (about 0.83 s in the air, so about 5 units at 6 units/s, enough to cross the jump pair's 3.5 units to the next rail); with the Jump power-up's tier 2 owned the launch uses its higher takeoff (8) instead, so the upgrade still means longer flights off a rail. Off the rail's end with Space still held the car flies on along the rail as before, stays tilted and can catch the next rail it touches (no launch: the launch is only letting go).
_tilt_comment: The tilt (T-551): 3 transition frames into the held pose, the same backwards when Space is let go in the air and on landing (the proposal: the tilt plays out on the ground as the car drives off, rather than snapping back). tilt_frame_seconds 0.06 is 3 physics steps per frame: each of the 3 frames is seen (at 2 steps the in-betweens flicker past), and the held pose is reached in 0.14 s, well inside a first-tier Jump's 0.83 s in the air.
_arrow_comment: The jump arrow (T-551; HUD and menus, Decisions, "The jump arrow"): shown while grinding (the launch is only possible on a rail), on by default (game_settings.gd). A flat arrowhead at the car's height just past its nose: its base arrow_distance units from the car's centre (the drawing is 1.5 to the nose, so 0.5 clear of it), arrow_length long and arrow_width wide (about a car's width: big enough to read, small enough not to cover the rail). Off-white with a dark outline at arrow_opacity, so it reads on the dark street and on the bar, in the Drift Guide's flat pixel look.
_effect_comment: The jump effect (T-551; Drifting, Decisions, "A jump effect around the car"): each play lasts jump_effect_seconds, about half a first-tier Jump's time in the air, so it is over before the car lands and never stacks with the next jump's.
_join_comment: Joints (T-542 round 2; the board: a joint between connected rail pieces at an angle must cost no speed, and long rails curve round corners built of angled pieces). Two rails are connected when an end of one is within join_distance units (flat) of the end the car leaves by and within join_height units of its height. The car then crosses straight onto the next piece, at the same speed (nothing lost to the angle), as long as that piece's way on turns the travel by no more than join_max_angle_deg (100: a right angle and a little over, never a fold back). All proposals for the board's playtest.
